'Société Anonyme' reserved exclusively for SA companies

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted; SARL requires a physical registered office address in France
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High likelihood of unannounced physical inspections by tax authorities for commercial substance verification and by commercial police for address compliance

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), Livre II, Titre II (Articles L. 223-1 to L. 223-42)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte de constitution de la société (statuts)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital of €1 fully subscribed and paid-up in cash upon share issuance; no escrow account required for SARL
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The initial shareholders of the proposed Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) unanimously resolve as follows: 1. Share subscription: The shareholders subscribe to shares totaling minimum capital of €1, fully paid in cash. 2. Registered office adoption: The registered office is established at [full French address]. 3. Officer appointments: [Name] is appointed Gérant (Manager) with full representation powers; [Name] is appointed Président if required. 4. Articles adoption: The articles of association are adopted in the presented form. This resolution is passed unanimously on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public and Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare statuts and subscription list; have acte de constitution notarized; ensure all details match proposed capital and officers.
required_dossiers: Identity documents (passport/ID), proof of address, draft statuts, share subscription list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Provide missing documents or amend within 15 days

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via guichet-entreprises.fr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit acte de constitution and statuts electronically or in person; obtain SIREN/SIRET numbers post-approval.
required_dossiers: Acte de constitution, statuts, identity proofs, proof of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any formal defects within 15 days or refile

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for SIREN, obtain RCS number, open corporate bank account, and register for VAT if applicable.
required_dossiers: SIREN certificate, bank details, corporate statutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Follow up with authorities for any delays

required_dossiers: Environmental declarations, fire safety application, structural inspection reports
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Address non-compliance notices within prescribed timelines

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No physical operations; remote work only. No wastewater, VOCs, or waste handling required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from local fire brigade, structural load inspections, and workplace safety clearance from labour inspectorate if office-based

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP), operating the impots.gouv.fr taxpayer portal and the professional space titled Le Compte Fiscal en Ligne (CFL). Company formation and tax identifier clearance are routed through the one-stop shop of the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI Guichet Unique); inscription is made in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; INSEE assigns the SIREN (9-digit national identification) and SIRET (site establishment identification) used as the official French tax identification references; DGFIP automatically issues the intra-Community VAT number to the registered SARL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The French SARL is a domestic tax resident and obtains its TIN/VAT ID without a separate discretionary application: file the incorporation dossier containing the signed statutes, registered office proof in France, appointment of the gérant, and legal publication certificate through the INPI Guichet Unique; INSEE then emits the SIREN/SIRET; DGFIP attributes the TVA intracommunautaire in the format FR + 2-digit control key + 9-digit SIREN. Non-resident corporate shareholders do not require a French TIN merely to hold SARL interests. A non-established foreign service provider or intra-group supplier that independently incurs French VAT obligations must apply through Cerfa form n 3527bis to the Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE) and, if located outside the EU, must additionally appoint a DGFIP-approved representative for value-added tax (CGI art. 289 A). The gérant must in parallel register for personal French income tax formalities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a French SARL is an autonomous legal entity subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) at the standard 25% rate; it is not fiscally transparent. Being resident in France by reason of legal seat and effective management, it is taxable on worldwide profits except profit attributable to foreign permanent establishments benefiting from an exemption clause under an applicable double-taxation treaty (territorial scope of treaty-based PE relief). The pass-through family undertaking election (SARL de famille) is not available because ownership is not confined to a close circle of natural persons in the required family relationship.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a check-the-box regime; classification follows the General Tax Code. Permit-granting elections relevant to the SARL include: (i) the parent-subsidiary tax regime (régime des sociétés mères, CGI art. 145) electable to benefit from a 95% participation exemption on dividends received from qualifying subsidiaries; (ii) the French tax consolidation option (intégration fiscale, CGI art. 223 A) for a French head company that owns at least 95% of French subsidiaries — a foreign parent must route consolidation through a French-resident intermediary; (iii) the VAT distinct taxable person election (assujetti unique, CGI art. 256 C III) allowing tightly linked French establishments to create a VAT group; and (iv) binding advance rulings (rescrit fiscal) to confirm the VAT place of supply of a BPO service, the existence of a permanent establishment, or the treatment of a cross-border payment. EU ATAD anti-hybrid rules are mandatory rather than elective: mismatched deductions, inclusions and double-deductions are automatically neutralized, and the taxpayer cannot opt out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA) — a destination-based, invoice-credit, multi-stage consumption tax implemented under EU Directive 2006/112/EC and codified in the Code Général des Impôts.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR — no turnover threshold applies to French-established enterprises: the SARL is a VAT taxable person from incorporation, although the small-business exemption (franchise en base, CGI art. 293 B) permits invoicing without VAT up to EUR 91,900 of annual turnover for goods and EUR 36,800 for services. For EU-established suppliers of remote digital services or distance-selling goods to French consumers the EU-wide cross-border threshold of EUR 10,000 applies; non-EU persons have zero threshold and become registrable from the first taxable French transaction unless the customer self-accounts under reverse charge. Inbound B2B services purchased by the SARL from foreign suppliers are governed by the reverse-charge mechanism in France, avoiding French registration of the foreign supplier.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is rolling out a mandatory e-invoicing and e-reporting reform (Finance Act 2024, decree n 2022-428 and implementing decrees). From 1 September 2026, all VAT-registered businesses must accept electronic invoices, and large and medium-sized enterprises must emit structured e-invoices; from 1 September 2027, small and micro-sized enterprises must emit them. Invoices must be issued in Factur-X (hybrid) or UBL/CII XML format, transmitted over a certified dematerialization platform (PDP) or the free public portal (PPF), with e-invoicing and e-reporting data passed to DGFIP for structured data matching and VAT return alignment. France does not impose real-time fiscal stamping or centralized government clearance technology; it uses structured continuous transmission and post-clearing audit. Sanctions of EUR 15 per non-compliant invoice (maximum EUR 15,000 per year) and EUR 250 per missing or erroneous e-reporting dataset (maximum EUR 15,000 per year) apply.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported outside the EU are exempt from French VAT with full right to deduct input VAT (de facto zero-rating) under CGI art. 262-I-1° and Annex II art. 74-0 C, provided the exporter holds proof that the goods left the EU within three months after the supply. For remote BPO and call-center services, no customs export zero-rating exists; the relevant rule is a supply-of-services displacement: when the customer is a taxable person (B2B), the place of supply is the customer's country (CGI art. 259-1), so the French SARL invoices without French VAT; an EU customer accounts for VAT under reverse charge and a non-EU customer is generally outside French VAT. When the call-center service is rendered to a non-taxable person located abroad, French VAT may still be due under the default B2C rule (CGI art. 259A), except electronically supplied services under CGI art. 259B whose place of supply is the consumer's country and which require OSS registration and reporting. Input VAT deduction is preserved for costs attributable to export, out-of-scope and reverse-charged revenues; full credit is typically available to the BPO operations as long as the supporting documentation identifies the foreign customer, the service performance and the payment flow.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (DAU / Déclaration en Douane) with Movement Reference Number (MRN) and destination customs office outside the EU
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill naming the French SARL as exporter and evidencing the port or airport of departure from the EU
Commercial invoice issued at 0% VAT with the applicable Incoterms and the statutory reference of the export exemption
Effective export proof such as a signed delivery note, arrival certificate or foreign customs stamp confirming arrival in the destination country
Inward Remittance Certificate or corresponding bank credit advice evidencing collection of the export receivable within the repatriation period
For services: executed BPO contract, statement of work, service delivery logs, client acceptance report, and remittance advices matching the invoiced amounts
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFIP may audit export and out-of-scope evidence for three years, extended to six years in cases of undisclosed activity or fiscal fraud. If the SARL fails to furnish admissible proof of export within three months, or if the zero-rating/out-of-scope treatment is found to be documentary-only or fraudulent, the VAT is prospectively and retrospectively reassessed: the previously credited or refunded VAT is clawed back together with statutory late-payment interest (intérêt de retard at 0.20% per month from the due date). Additional penalties escalate from 40% for deliberate misstatement (manquement délibéré) to 80% for fraudulent maneuvers or abuse of law (manœuvres frauduleuses, abus de droit) and 100% for opposition to tax control; criminal prosecution under CGI art. 1741 may result in five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine, or seven years and EUR 3,000,000 in aggravated circumstances. The appointed tax representative and the gérant of the SARL incur joint and several liability for the company's VAT debts and penalties under CGI arts. 1754–1755, and corporate criminal liability can additionally be imposed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders' meeting decision approving the SARL financial statements and discharging the manager (procès-verbal d'assemblée générale ordinaire)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minute book kept at the registered office; copy retained in the commercial registry file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the fiscal year end (for a 31 December year-end, by 30 June of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the approval meeting within the statutory period exposes the company to a court-ordered injunction, an ad hoc mandate at the shareholders' request, and irregularity of subsequent registry filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts (bilan, compte de résultat, annexes) and management report with the trade and companies register (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce — Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after the shareholders' approval decision and in any event by 6 months after the fiscal year close (for a 31 December year-end, by 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-deposit triggers a formal notice, then a court order with a coercive daily fine (astreinte); after one year of continued default, the registry may initiate administrative strike-off and dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale) — Form 2065-SD together with schedules 2053 to 2058-SD
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year SARL, by the 4th calendar month after fiscal year end (30 April for a 31 December year-end); non-calendar-year taxpayers file within 4 months of fiscal close. Online filing is mandatory.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 5% late penalty on corporate income tax assessed, increasing to 10% after 30 days, plus monthly interest at 0.2% of unpaid tax; additional fixed penalties may apply to the liasse requirement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual CVAE turnover statement (Form 1330-CVAE) for SARLs whose gross turnover exceeds the French statutory threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year taxpayer, by 3 May of the following year, extended to the next business day if 3 May falls on a weekend or bank holiday
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a 10% supplement on the CVAE assessment after 15 days plus monthly interest; persistent failure may lead to a tax authority assessment ex officio.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Update and annual accuracy review of the register of beneficial owners (UBO register) — Form 1477-SD where a shareholding change occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce — Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any transfer of shares, change in control, or other change in beneficial ownership; no separate fixed anniversary filing is imposed by French law
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update the UBO register within the legal period gives rise to civil sanction proceedings and may be treated as a compliance defect in the RCS record; repeated omission can support strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A French SARL must appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) at the annual general meeting if, at the fiscal year end, it exceeds at least two of the three following thresholds: (i) total balance sheet assets exceeding €4,000,000; (ii) net turnover exclusive of VAT exceeding €8,000,000; (iii) average number of permanent employees exceeding 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général) as issued by the Autorité des Normes Comptables for the individual statutory accounts of the SARL; IFRS as endorsed in the European Union applies to consolidated accounts if the entity is part of a group required to prepare consolidated financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a stand-alone annual UBO re-filing. The SARL has a continuous obligation to keep the register of beneficial owners at the registered office and to file Form 1477-SD with the commercial registry within 30 days of any share transfer or ownership change. At each annual accounts approval meeting, management must review the register against current shareholding to ensure accuracy; a decision confirming the register may be included in the minutes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - 2,000 annually for a professional domiciliation or virtual registered-office service in France
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - 18,000 for a typical small or medium-sized SARL when a certified statutory audit is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, CGI)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on the first €42,000 of annual taxable profit for SMEs satisfying turnover ≤ €10,000,000 and paid-in capital conditions; no territorial or cash-based incentive for BPO; research credit CIR not applicable to call centre activities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory expiry; annual utilization capped at €1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profits exceeding €1,000,000)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cerfa 2065 (liasse fiscale 2065 with ancillary schedules 2050–2067) filed electronically via the impots.gouv.fr tele-declaration 'EFi-Méga' service or via an EDI-certified accounting software channel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (same as the accounting fiscal year), with mandatory monthly VAT returns and annual collective labour declarations concurrent with the business activity.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year closed on 31 December: by 3 May of the following calendar year. For a fiscal year ending otherwise: no later than three months after the closure date. All declarations must be e-filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover exclusive of VAT generated from BPO helpdesk and tele-sales contracts (including multilingual support, outbound campaigns and remote infrastructure fees).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only French-sourced revenue allocated to the French operation; attach intercompany documentation showing the seat-based/per-minute arm's length rate and the foreign parent re-invoicing policy.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses: payroll for call agents and managers, telecom costs, software/telecom SaaS expenditures, rent, utilities, professional fees and outbound tele-sales telecom costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to non-resident related parties are deductible only to the extent that France's thin-capitalisation, abusive-cost and transfer pricing rules are satisfied; written contracts and a transfer pricing study must be held.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss before taxes after recognition of all provisions and depreciation (tableau 2051).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident managers must ensure the result reflects the commercial reality of the French SARL; a persistent loss position with intercompany profit booked abroad will automatically trigger Article 57 CGI re-invoicing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule providing separate listing of tax adjustments: non-deductible fines, excessive director remuneration, C3S participation tax, and transfer pricing restitution to the foreign parent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent intercompany management fees must be supported by a service agreement with demonstrable service; lack of invoices and proof of receipt will lead to rejection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of previous tax losses carried forward and deducted against taxable income for the current year, subject to the statutory cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The deductibility should be computed under French rules even if the foreign parent consolidates; a statement of loss history must be transmitted; no loss surrender to shareholders is allowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (or deficit) after integration of all adjustments, used for the computation of corporate income tax and the 25% withholding tax on distribution.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The final fiscal result must be signed by the legal representative; non-resident directors are advised to review for consistency with the ledger and TP structures before tele-submission on 3 May.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an automatic 10% penalty on the net corporate tax due plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.20% (Article 1731 CGI); after a formal notice (mise en demeure), failure within 30 days triggers a 40% intentional misstatement penalty; deliberate concealment or abuse of right leads to an 80% penalty. Incorrectly completed e-filing is subject to a €15 per-line error fine and possible €250 per-week coercive fine.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Article 119 bis(2) CGI on gross dividends paid to a non-French corporate shareholder; domestic law provides no exemption except treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a tax treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, the foreign beneficial owner must submit to the French paying agent or the DGFiP: Form 5000 (treaty residence certificate) or Form 5087 for the EU Directive, a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) issued for the calendar year, evidence of beneficial ownership, holding percentage and 24-month holding period, together with Form 5000's declaration of personal residence. The request must be filed prior to the payment date; otherwise, excess WHT can be recovered through a refund claim within three years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate for IP royalties (patents, trademarks, copyrights) and technical-know-how paid to non-residents: 25% (Article 182 B CGI), with treaty reductions generally to 5% or 10%; qualifying EU associated companies may claim 0% under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive. Cross-border interest paid to non-resident commercial lenders: no statutory French WHT if the loan is fully documented and booked through a French debtor; a 25% WHT applies to bond or non-bank loan interest received by non-residents outside treaty protection; treaty rates commonly 0%-10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 group consolidated annual revenue (after elimination of intra-group sales) triggers mandatory Local File / Master File under Article L.13 AA LPF; CbC Report is required when the consolidated group revenue exceeds EUR 750,000,000; an entity with cross-border related party transactions less than EUR 50,000 annual flow may file a simplified form 2257-TD but must retain documentary evidence upon audit.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no standalone Economic Substance Regulation akin to the Gulf regimes; nevertheless the abuse-of-law doctrine (Article L.64 LPF) permits the DGFiP to disregard transactions and corporate vehicles lacking genuine economic substance, genuine premises, employees and business purpose. A French SARL acting as an empty booking hub while the BPO directors, risk functions and servers are abroad is recharacterised as artificially transferring profits, leading to re-integration, withholding and abstention penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately failing to file the Cerfa 2065, filing an all-zero declaration for a French call centre which produces income, or channelling French BPO proceeds into a personal foreign account while reporting fictitious cost bases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-instatement of the French taxable base, 0.20% monthly late interest, 10% automatic late-filing penalty, 40% penalty for intentional misstatement, 80% enhancement for abusive concealment; criminal prosecution of tax evasion carries a fine up to €500,000 and imprisonment of five years (Article 1741 CGI).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Article L.267 LPF, directors who directly and knowingly participate in the tax fraud may be held jointly liable for the company's taxes; criminal conviction leads to personal fines, travel bans, freezing of personal assets and disqualification from managing French businesses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming the SARL as an artificial intermediary that only concentrates margin while the genuine call-handling servers, managers and staff are entirely outside France, with the SARL lacking fixed business premises, dedicated local officers and any local profit-producing activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Deduction of management fees, telecom re-charges and software royalties is denied; a 25% constructive dividend withholding is applied to the whole shifted margin; abuse-of-law penalty of 80%; under commercial insolvency law the company may be liquidated as a fictitious structure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors risk the 'action en comblement du passif' in judicial liquidation; the court can impose a ban on exercising commercial activity, up to 10 years, and a travel restriction; in the criminal branch, participation is treated as aggravated tax fraud with imprisonment and fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Invoicing BPO services from the SARL to a related foreign parent below arm's-length price per call-minute or chatbot transaction; deliberate non-contemporaneous documentation; fictitious cost-allocations and omission of the 2257-TD declaration despite an operational intra-group flow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administration corrects the transaction under Article 57 CGI, upwardly adjusting the French profit at 25%, plus monthly interest 0.20% and a 40% penalty for serious misevaluation; further indirect tax consequences: VAT re-characterisation and potential denial of input VAT recovery on procurement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers who signed or ratified transfer pricing returns without a reasonable basis may be personally reassessed for penalties; in the event of default, they are conjoined debtor in respect of 40% penalties; a court may declare them personally liable in the payment of the company's tax liabilities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using unregistered Wise Business or wire transfers for BPO receivables without obtaining the required KYC declarations, artificially creating intercompany debts to justify rapid onward payments to non-EU shell companies, or failing to report suspicious client deposit patterns to Tracfin.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Breach of the French Monetary and Financial Code: administrative fine up to €5,000,000 or 5% of turnover, penal sanction for money laundering up to five years' imprisonment and a fine of €375,000; asset freeze, confiscation, and a prohibition from providing financial or commercial services for up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors found to have knowingly routed fraudulent or disguised funds face personal criminal liability, restitution orders to affected clients, civil damages, international travel bans and disqualification from corporate directorship across the EU.
